label: rem:q-dilogarithm-pentagon-associator
title: The $q$-dilogarithm pentagon as the monoidal associator axiom
html:
The q-dilogarithm is not imported into the framework as a separate datum; it is the solution of a coherence condition the substrate category \mathbf{C} already carries. Because \mathbf{C} is monoidal, its associator \alpha_{X,Y,Z}\colon (X\otimes Y)\otimes Z \to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z) satisfies the Mac Lane pentagon coherence — the five reassociations of a fourfold tensor commute. Passing to the shuffle Hopf algebra \mathcal{H}_q of the braiding, that coherence descends to a functional equation on the level-2 shuffle primitive: the five reassociations collapse to the five-term relation

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(y) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q(x) = \mathrm{Li}_2^q(xy) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\left(\frac{x(1-y)}{1-xy}\right) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\left(\frac{y(1-x)}{1-xy}\right).

By def:q-dilogarithm there is exactly one level-2 primitive satisfying this relation, so the pentagon axiom names \mathrm{Li}_2^q rather than merely constraining it — the dilogarithm is the unique scalar shadow of the associator. In operator form this is the Faddeev–Kashaev identity: the quantum dilogarithm is the quantum associator (equivalently the 6j-symbol), and the operator pentagon

  \Phi(\mathsf P)\,\Phi(\mathsf Q) = \Phi(\mathsf Q)\,\Phi(\mathsf P+\mathsf Q)\,\Phi(\mathsf P)

on a Weyl pair \mathsf P\mathsf Q = \mathsf Q\mathsf P + 1 is the same coherence read as a fusion move.

Two links in that reading are not formalised, and the scope boundary of prop:dilog-pentagon-is-associator records both. What is proved there is the scalar equivalence: a potential on \mathcal{H}_q satisfies the five-term relation exactly when it is a q-dilogarithm datum. The descent from the morphism-level Mac Lane pentagon on \alpha_{X,Y,Z} to that scalar equation is the classical shuffle--associator identification of Faddeev--Kashaev, cited rather than machine-checked; and the analytic five-term relation at q \neq 1 remains a conjecture class. So the pentagon names \mathrm{Li}_2^q within the scalar layer, and the passage from the categorical axiom to that layer rests on the cited identification.

Two faces of the one associator. On the substrate branch (real q) the pentagon is realised by the compact dilogarithm \Phi_q / \mathrm{Li}_2^q — the bar-even face that drives mass and binding. Continued to the fibre branch |q|=1, where the compact product's zeros accumulate on the unit circle and it ceases to be well defined, the surviving realisation is Faddeev's non-compact modular double \Phi_b = \Phi_{1/b} (with q = e^{2\pi i b^2}) — the bar-odd face carrying the decay observable. Both solve the same pentagon; they are the two archimedean lenses of prop:phi-q-aj-machinery-identification (real versus root-of-unity saddle of the one \hat{A}_K), not two different objects.

The observable is a pairing, not a product. Where an archimedean number is finally extracted, the dilogarithm associator enters as an analytic operator paired against the algebraic Markov-trace state — a Hopf–Drinfeld pairing (equivalently a q-difference-module action), not a scalar multiplication: the continuous flow is contracted against the finite cyclotomic trace data. This "analytic paired with algebraic" structure fixes the shape of the observable. It does not, by itself, determine the analytic monodromy datum away from the roots of unity — that datum is genuinely resurgent and remains open.
